A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mechanistic PDE Networks work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable across the conference reformatting, including retained Appendices A–B and new Appendix C.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original numerical experiments on PDE discovery, noise robustness, and Laplace solver accuracy.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Section 6.3 and Appendix C add solver sensitivity, runtime, and GPU-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The encoder, PDE parameterization, differentiable solver, discovery losses, and multigrid-preconditioned FGMRES procedure are retained. Appendix B changes 'GMRES' to 'FGMRES', aligning its description with Section 3.1 in both versions.

E1.justification: Both evaluate diffusion, viscous and inviscid Burgers, porous-medium, easy and hard reaction-diffusion, Navier–Stokes, and Laplace problems. Appendix C reuses Laplace for solver-parameter and resolution sweeps, without adding a distinct task or data domain.

E2.justification: PDEFIND and WeakSINDy remain the reaction-diffusion comparators; WeakSINDy remains the Navier–Stokes and Burgers comparator. The Laplace unit test retains py-pde as its reference. The added solver analyses introduce no comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds controlled Laplace evaluation protocols using relative linear-system error and sweeps of FGMRES iterations, V-cycles, and Gauss–Seidel steps. Captions specify 20 FGMRES restarts and batch size 32 for resource profiling. Existing discovery protocols and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix C introduce a substantive solver-focused analysis absent from v1: sensitivity to three iterative-solver controls and runtime/memory scaling with resolution. This extends the analysis beyond the retained Laplace accuracy check and discovery-noise robustness experiments.

E5.justification: The porous-medium estimate remains 2.64 ± 0.03. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised; the new solver curves and resource measurements introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 8–10 add convergence and sensitivity curves, while Figure 11 adds measured computational costs: 1.6, 4.63, and 16.7 GB and 6.16, 13.9, and 33.9 seconds for batch-32 Laplace solves on 32x32, 64x64, and 128x128 grids. This substantially expands quantitative solver characterization. Existing discovery results and Laplace unit-test errors are retained; these are additional measurements, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The well-posedness assumption, constrained formulation, least-squares and differentiation derivations, and multigrid algorithm are unchanged. Section 2 corrects an illustrative index from x1x1 to x1x2 to match the already-listed mixed derivative; this is a notation correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: differentiable parallel PDE solving and discovery of nonlinear equations with noise robustness. The new solver evidence supports existing claims without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of noise performance and Navier–Stokes false positives remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning scalability, speed versus accuracy, and identifiability. The new solver discussion reports empirical trends, and the added impact statement supplies no substantive qualification.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a repository address with a promise of future source-code availability. Appendix C documents controls for the new solver experiments, including restart counts, iteration/V-cycle settings, and profiling batch size. The PDFs do not establish an actual code release.

R1.justification: Section 5 retains the same prior work and positioning relative to neural solvers, physics-informed networks, SINDy variants, and mechanistic networks. The bibliography is reformatted without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized wording and notation corrections, brief new Section 6.3 and Appendix C, expanded acknowledgements, and a generic impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Figure 7 moves from Appendix A into the main text. Appendix C adds three plots and the resource table labeled Figure 11.

improvement.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix C strengthen practical assessment of the solver through controlled sensitivity tests and measured runtime/memory costs, supplementing v1's accuracy check and dense-storage estimates. The existing discovery evidence remains intact. The gain is limited because the new analyses concern Laplace alone, omit hardware identification and uncertainty reporting, and the code announcement remains prospective.
